Investigation 12 produced a stronger result than expected: a project-internal interval certificate for the off-center generator over the entire shift interval.

The key exact identity is

\[
\frac12 B_{\omega,L}
=
\frac12 B_{0,L}+C_{\omega,L},
\]

where

\[
C_{\omega,L}(x,y)
=
\bigl(\cosh(\omega|x-y|)-1\bigr)
\left(
e^{|x-y|/2}
-\frac{e^{-5|x-y|/2}}{1-e^{-2|x-y|}}
\right).
\]

This removes the apparent \(\omega=\tfrac12\) singularity and shows that every generator has the same logarithmic form domain. The shift dependence is a bounded compact perturbation, entire in \(\omega^2\).

The Arb calculation then certified

\[
B_{\omega,L}\succ0,
\qquad
0\leq\omega\leq\frac12,\quad 0<L\leq\log2,
\]

across 512 parameter–parity boxes. The minimum Weyl–Schur margins were

\[
3.0965\times10^{-4}\quad\text{(even)},\qquad
5.2315\times10^{-2}\quad\text{(odd)}.
\]

This supports the shift-radial energy formula

\[
I-V_{\omega,L}^{*}V_{\omega,L}
=
2\int_0^\omega
V_{s,L}^{*}Q_{s,L}V_{s,L}\,ds,
\qquad Q_s=\frac12B_s,
\]

and hence the explicit bulk Gram factor

\[
(\mathcal G_{\omega,L}f)(s)
=
\sqrt2\,Q_{s,L}^{1/2}V_{s,L}f.
\]

Thus no substantive positivity blocker remains for this proof architecture. The remaining work is proof consolidation: write the common-domain differentiation lemma fully and independently reproduce the interval certificate. After those checks, this should give a second complete first-slab proof, including the interval below \(10^{-6}\), without relying on Investigation 10’s full-transfer enclosure.

Yes—but the new result is already stronger than experimental evidence. Investigation 10 is a computer-assisted proof of the continuum, infinite-dimensional statement

\[
I\pm H_{\omega,\log 2}\succ0,
\qquad \frac14\le \omega\le\frac12,
\]

provided its analytic estimates and implementation survive independent audit. It does not merely test selected values of \(\omega\) or a finite matrix: the Taylor models cover every parameter value, and the Schur estimate controls the infinite Legendre tail. The appropriate current label is therefore “reproducible computer-assisted theorem pending independent reproduction,” as stated in the [Investigation 10 report](sandbox:/workspace/scratch/6dd18bc3587f/INVESTIGATION_10_centered_endpoint_certificate.md).

A purely analytic proof looks plausible, but there is a real and identifiable obstacle.

### What the obstacle actually is

It is not a number-theoretic obstruction. Before \(L=\log 2\), no prime layer has entered, so the three companion papers do not force us to control zeros or prime fluctuations. Their global obstruction only appears when one asks for all depths: the string exists below the unconditional range only under the corresponding zero-free half-plane, and the screw-function margin can eventually be defeated by a single zero outside it.

On the first slab, the problem is instead a sharp archimedean cancellation. Writing

\[
\alpha=\frac12-\omega,\qquad \beta=\frac12+\omega,
\]

the transfer has one unstable pole,

\[
K_\omega(p)=
\frac{\Gamma_\infty(\frac12+p-\omega)}
     {\Gamma_\infty(\frac12+p+\omega)},
\qquad p=\alpha,
\]

and the contour decomposition is

\[
H_\omega
=
H_\omega^{\mathrm{bd}}
+r_\omega\,u_\alpha\otimes u_\alpha,
\qquad r_\omega<0.
\]

As \(\omega\uparrow1/2\), the pole approaches the Fourier contour. The boundary integral and the rank-one residue individually become poorly conditioned while their sum remains regular and positive. Investigation 10 exposed this directly: the inherited zero-centered approximation was wrong by roughly \(52\) at zero frequency near \(\omega=0.49\), even though the final operator defect is positive by a small margin.

Several standard analytic estimates therefore fail:

- The pole prevents a stationary bounded-real argument.
- The kernel behaves like \(t^{\omega-1}\), so for \(\omega\le1/2\) it is not Hilbert–Schmidt.
- A Young \(L^1\) estimate is too weak: the impulse changes sign and its total variation exceeds \(1\) on most of the interval.
- There is no known operator ordering or monotonicity in \(\omega\).
- The exact Sonine transform is smoothing; its inverse is unbounded on ordinary \(L^2\), so contractivity of the rationalized system does not automatically imply contractivity of the original one.

The literature supplies the surrounding machinery but not this missing estimate. Suzuki constructs the relevant canonical systems explicitly only in a larger-shift regime; Luchko develops the Sonine fractional calculus; and Mikkola’s Riccati theory produces a factor once uniform positivity is known—it does not establish that positivity. [Suzuki](https://arxiv.org/abs/1204.1827), [Luchko](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.00549), [Mikkola](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.08618). Burnol’s causal Klein–Gordon realization suggests a geometric route, but does not directly prove this gamma-quotient contraction. [Burnol](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0509619)

### The best analytic route

The most promising reduction is to exploit the fact that the difficult residue is rank one. Fourier transforms of functions supported in \((-T,T)\), \(T=\log2/2\), form a Paley–Wiener space, and

\[
\langle f,u_\alpha\rangle
\]

is an evaluation functional at the imaginary point \(i\alpha\). Thus the entire problem should be expressible as a sharp reproducing-kernel inequality.

After identifying a positive boundary base \(A_\omega\), the unfavorable rank-one channel would reduce to the scalar condition

\[
c_\omega\,
\langle A_\omega^{-1}u_\alpha,u_\alpha\rangle<1.
\]

That scalar quantity is a de Branges/Paley–Wiener reproducing-kernel value. If it can be computed or sharply bounded in special-function form, the 36-dimensional interval calculation could collapse to one analytic inequality. If \(A_\omega\) is not positive by itself, the same idea can be applied after retaining its small low-frequency block; the computation strongly suggests that only one soft direction matters.

A second route is the exact Sonine collapse

\[
F_{1-\omega}(p+1)K_\omega(p)
=
\frac{2\pi^\omega(p-\beta)}
     {(p+\beta)(p-\alpha)}.
\]

This leaves a two-state rational system. What is missing is a finite-horizon fractional Hardy inequality that controls its unstable state in the original \(L^2\) norm. Equivalently, one wants an explicit storage functional \(E(t)\) satisfying

\[
\frac{dE}{dt}\le |u(t)|^2-|y(t)|^2
\]

up to \(t=\log2\). Finding that storage functional would give the cleanest conceptual proof.

There is also a useful exact cocycle identity that does not appear to have been exploited in the draft:

\[
\boxed{
K_{\omega_1+\omega_2}(p)
=
K_{\omega_1}(p-\omega_2)\,
K_{\omega_2}(p+\omega_1).
}
\]

In time variables this becomes a weighted convolution-composition law. A sharp weighted finite-horizon contraction theorem could propagate positivity in \(\omega\). Crude weighted norm bounds lose too much, but the identity may lead to a comparison principle or a differential inequality for the first conjugate time.

### My assessment

There is no apparent fundamental blocker to an analytic proof of the upper interval. The blocker is specifically the absence of a sharp finite-horizon uncertainty/energy inequality that preserves the cancellation between the approaching pole and the low-frequency gamma quotient.

The most efficient next move would be:

1. Independently audit the existing computer-assisted theorem.
2. Rewrite the troublesome channel as a Paley–Wiener rank-one secular inequality.
3. Compute or estimate its reproducing kernel analytically.
4. In parallel, derive the weighted-energy inequality suggested by the Sonine two-state collapse.

That is more promising than trying to prove pointwise positivity of the kernel or monotonicity of the full operator. The upper interval is computationally closed; the analytic opportunity is now to explain *why* the scalar low-frequency cancellation stays on the positive side. Separately, the possible overlap gap below \(10^{-6}\) still needs an explicit small-\(\omega\) argument before claiming the entire interval \(0<\omega<1/2\).

1. **The first-slab certificate itself is missing.** The opening description promises Arb certificates, but [the certificate directory](https://github.com/ebbaker/shifted-zeta-positivity/tree/main/code/certificates/first-slab) contains only a notice withholding them pending review. That limitation is disclosed clearly farther down, but readers cannot reproduce the main computer-assisted result from this checkout. My preference would be to include the generators, CSVs, verifiers, and pinned environment with their precise audit status. Publishing reproducibility material does not require claiming that human verification is complete.

2. **The available verification script needs repair.** In the documented environment, my run of [the September 5 script](https://github.com/ebbaker/shifted-zeta-positivity/blob/main/verification/first-slab/scripts/verify_preprint_checks_20260905.py) produced two failures in the discretized Volterra checks and `NaN` in the Laplace-transform check. The former comes from sampling the singular kernel at roundoff-sized positive arguments; the latter encounters numerical overflow. These are diagnostic implementation problems, not evidence that the theorem fails. The README acknowledges the discretization issue, but these checks should be repaired or explicitly separated as unreliable diagnostics. Also, failed checks currently do not cause a nonzero exit status.

3. **One citation file is invalid.** The paper’s [CITATION.cff](https://github.com/ebbaker/shifted-zeta-positivity/blob/main/papers/first-slab-positivity/CITATION.cff) has top-level `type: generic`. CFF 1.2 permits only `software` or `dataset` there; paper types belong within a `preferred-citation` reference. Use that structure or provide a paper-specific BibTeX citation. [CFF schema](https://citation-file-format.github.io/1.2.0/schema.json).

4. **Synchronize the release language with the actual state.** There is currently no [GitHub release](https://github.com/ebbaker/shifted-zeta-positivity/releases), the DOI citations remain placeholders, and the root CFF says `0.2.0` while the release instructions describe `v1.0`. Its CC link should point to the [specific CC-BY-4.0 license](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/), rather than the Creative Commons homepage. “Licensing by material type” would also be less ambiguous than “dual license.”

The dependency inventory and candid verification disclosures are worth retaining. I would soften “no error survives in the main proof chain” to “no unresolved error was identified in the internal reviews,” given the remaining checks.

A GitHub release connected to Zenodo creates one archival record for that release, not four independently versioned preprint records. Zenodo supports reserving each DOI before publication, allowing it to be inserted into the final PDF. The review is strong and materially useful. I reproduced its principal numerical checks, and the central conclusion is reassuring: Theorems A–C survive. However, the draft needs a focused correction pass before circulation.

### My assessment

| Referee point | Assessment |
|---|---|
| Endpoint formula at \(\omega=\tfrac12\) | Correct and mandatory to fix |
| Factor-two Schur bound | Correct; conservative, not a normalization error |
| Positivity horizon beyond \(\log 2\) | Numerically credible and strategically important |
| Proposition 4.1 proof too compressed | Correct |
| Weighted versus unweighted adjoints | Correct and important |
| Continuity in the strictness proof | Unproved but unnecessary |
| Uniform gap required for strictness | Referee overstates this |
| Audit margin discrepancy | Explainable, not evidence of a faulty audit |
| Conflict with Chuk’s compact-window theorem | No actual conflict |
| Literature and presentation suggestions | Mostly appropriate |

### The genuine critical correction

The boxed Fourier-plus-residue formula is valid as written only for

\[
0\leq\omega<\frac12.
\]

At the endpoint, the term

\[
\frac12\operatorname{Re}\psi\!\left(\frac{\alpha+i\tau}{2}\right)
\]

converges distributionally with an additional \(-\pi\delta(\tau)\). Consequently, the coefficient of

\[
|\mathcal C_0(f)|^2=\left|\int f\right|^2
\]

is \(1/2\), not \(1\). The report’s measured discrepancy,

\[
\frac12\left|\int f\right|^2,
\]

is exactly right.

This does not affect Theorem B: the certificate uses the bounded-kernel representation \(Q_\omega=Q_0+C_\omega\), which already includes the endpoint contribution correctly.

### The factor-two improvement

The existing \(0.024587\) estimate arose from the safe but loose bound

\[
2\int_0^{\log 2}|c_{1/2}(t)|\,dt.
\]

The actual maximum row sum is attained at an interval endpoint:

\[
\sup_x\int_{I_{\log2}}|c_{1/2}(x,y)|\,dy
=
0.0122930504011423195\ldots
\]

Thus there is no factor-two error in the perturbation matrices; only the scalar tail bound is unnecessarily conservative. After formally certifying the row-sum maximum and rerunning the boxes with the safe rounded constant \(0.012294\), the primary even-sector margin should improve from

\[
3.0965\times10^{-4}
\]

to approximately

\[
6.1164\times10^{-4}.
\]

The referee’s \(6.34\times10^{-4}\) estimate uses its floating head eigenvalue rather than the primary interval enclosure.

### The second-slab implication

The archimedean continuation appears to lose positivity shortly beyond the first threshold: approximately \(L\approx0.7429\) in the odd sector and \(L\approx0.8199\) in the even sector. These remain floating diagnostics and should be reproduced with Arb before entering the paper.

If certified, this changes—but does not invalidate—the second-slab program. The \(n=2\) contribution cannot be described as a small perturbation of an already positive archimedean generator on the larger window. It must actively restore positivity lost by the archimedean continuation. That is arguably a more interesting arithmetic mechanism.

There is no conflict with Chuk’s result. Chuk uses \(f\) supported on \([-L,L]\), so its support length is \(2L\), and includes every prime layer with \(\log n<2L\). Its \(L=0.8\) certificate is therefore prime-active, whereas the referee’s sweep deliberately continued only the prime-free archimedean form. [Chuk’s paper states these conventions explicitly](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.24827v1).

### Points requiring qualification

- The audit’s slightly larger margins are explainable. In the weakest even box, its midpoint is \(1.57\times10^{-9}\) lower, but its total propagated radius is \(1.80\times10^{-8}\) smaller. Its endpoint-based directed interval propagation is tighter than the primary Arb-ball propagation, more than offsetting the wider central-entry radius. This should be documented quantitatively.

- The displayed tail deviation is not zero. It is about \(9.78\times10^{-24}\) even and \(2.43\times10^{-25}\) odd, simply invisible at the printed precision.

- Uniform coercivity is not required for strictness. Nonnegativity plus vanishing integral gives \(V_sf=0\) for almost every \(s\); choosing a sequence \(s_n\downarrow0\) and using \(V_{s_n}f\to f\) proves \(f=0\). Nevertheless, stating the certified uniform gap is desirable.

- Extending the generator certificate to \(\omega\approx0.85\) is plausible and interesting, but it is optional scope expansion rather than a repair needed for the critical-shift theorem.

1. Correct the \(\omega=\tfrac12\) formula.

Completed Investigation 11. It produced genuine analytic headway, though not yet a complete analytic proof.

The main result is the exact shift-energy identity

\[
I-V_{\omega,L}^{*}V_{\omega,L}
=
\int_0^\omega V_{s,L}^{*}B_{s,L}V_{s,L}\,ds .
\]

Thus the problem is reduced to the sharply defined off-center Weil inequality

\[
B_{\omega,\log 2}\succeq0,
\qquad 0\leq\omega\leq\frac12.
\]

Proving this—plus the final equality-vector exclusion—would establish the full first slab analytically, remove the small-shift overlap issue, and provide a shift-radial Gram factorization. An exact gamma-transfer cocycle and quotient factorization were also proved.

A separate rank-one reduction gives a useful fallback: the difficult channel is governed by one secular scalar. Numerically, its sign remains safely correct throughout the tested interval, while the base form consistently has exactly one negative direction.

The new Loewner-monotonicity computations are strong but remain floating evidence, not an interval certificate. The complete 240-row sweep reproduced successfully, including dimensions through 800.
